item.problem_title: Identification of dynamic regimes in continuous time under treatment-dependent observation is unresolved
item.problem_statement: Treatments, outcomes and clinical observations occur asynchronously and are recorded at times determined by the care process. Discretizing that onto a grid can reverse the temporal ordering of a treatment and an outcome falling in the same interval, merge several events into one, and define an estimand that exists only relative to the chosen interval. Identification and efficient estimation for dynamic interventions in continuous time under counting-process filtrations and irregular monitoring have been established. They do not yet settle the case an emulation on routine data actually faces: a visit process that depends on treatment, combined with effects that occur inside an interval. item.evidence: The paper identifies exactly when discretization is most damaging: when the treatment is an intermittent discrete action and the key time-varying confounder is itself a discrete event that the treatment affects almost instantaneously, so coarsening merges the two and mislabels which came first. That is the temporal-ordering failure the entry describes, characterized rather than asserted, and shown to be separate from unmeasured confounding.

item.problem_title: Emulation assumes no interference, and cloning individuals can produce joint strategies nobody could implement
item.problem_statement: One person's treatment can change another's outcome through infection, provider behavior, household exposure or a shared resource constraint. Target trial emulation as normally practiced invokes no interference, and under that assumption an individual-level protocol is coherent. Identifying a direct or spillover effect requires more than adding the interference literature alongside it: the emulation has to specify a feasible joint or stochastic treatment policy, the exposure mapping or potential-outcome indexing that defines what each unit is exposed to, and joint support for that exposure. item.paper: G-Formula for Observational Studies under Stratified Interference, with Application to Bed Net Use on Malaria
item.evidence: The entry says interference-aware emulation needs a feasible joint or stochastic policy, an exposure mapping and joint support, and that individual clone-censor rules do not identify those effects. This supplies exactly that machinery for partial interference: the exposure is cluster coverage, the estimands are overall and treated-specific effects at stated coverage levels, and the g-formula version works where the weighted estimators fail at large cluster sizes. item.quote: Inverse probability weighted estimators have previously been developed for observational studies with partial interference. verdicts.reason: The paper supplies a cluster-level causal framework with an explicit coverage intervention, which addresses part of the policy-intervention specification problem. item.problem_title: Emulation is proposed for non-pharmaceutical and policy interventions whose treatment versions and assignment units are not defined
item.problem_statement: Interference, combination therapies, multiple treatment versions and non-pharmaceutical interventions all strain the two-arm, individually assigned, well-defined-intervention assumptions the standard emulation protocol makes. Policy interventions are the sharpest case: delivered to a place or an organization rather than a person, varying in content by implementer, arriving gradually rather than on a date, and often with no comparable version of not receiving them. A policy emulation therefore has to specify the assignment unit, the timing, the comparator, the intervention versions or a stochastic rule over them, the exposure mapping under interference, and a cluster-level estimand. item.problem_title: An unobservable protocol component produces a different, data-defined estimand rather than a noisy version of the intended one
item.problem_statement: The canonical protocol has seven linked components: eligibility, treatment strategies, assignment, follow-up, outcomes, causal contrast and analysis plan. Conceptual specification and operational realization are distinct, and when a component cannot be observed the analyst substitutes a proxy. If no valid measurement, missing-data or validation model recovers the intended variable, the resulting observed-data functional generally does not identify the intended causal effect, and it does not automatically identify some other one either: naming it a different estimand requires a corresponding intervention and an identification argument. A criterion that cannot be verified is dropped and the population changes; a strategy that cannot be distinguished from its neighbor is merged and the contrast changes; an outcome that is only partly captured redefines the endpoint. item.problem_title: Positivity diagnostics describe weights instead of naming which patient histories are unsupported
item.problem_statement: A deterministic treatment strategy can assign a treatment that clinicians almost never give to patients with certain covariate histories. The standard response is to inspect the weight distribution and truncate the tail. Truncation is bias-variance regularization: it cannot identify an effect where the treatment density is structurally zero, and a marginal weight summary does not say which intervention-relevant histories carry small or zero density. What a reader needs and does not get is a policy-specific support criterion fixed in advance, diagnostics localized by time and by history, the fraction of the target population that fails the criterion, and the estimand that survives once those strata are set aside. Empirically, poor overlap has been shown to defeat adjustment methods that were otherwise well specified, which is the failure a weight histogram is least able to show. Software

item.problem_title: Registrations record the final protocol and not the alternatives that were rejected
item.problem_statement: An emulation makes many defensible decisions: active comparator, washout period, time zero, grace period, how treatment episodes are constructed, censoring rules, follow-up length and outcome definition. Each has more than one reasonable answer, and the set of answers is the researcher's degrees of freedom. Design guidance exists and states that the operational methods remain scenario dependent, so it narrows the set without closing it. Registrations record the specification that was finally run and not the alternatives considered, the order in which decisions were made, or which were revised after the data were inspected. A final protocol snapshot cannot reveal what was never logged, so a reader cannot distinguish a protocol written once from one converged upon, and no later audit can reconstruct it.

item.problem_statement: Prescriptions differ from dispensings and dispensings differ from ingestion; diagnostic codes differ from clinical events; death and care outside the system may be incompletely captured. An erroneous weight factor persists in the cumulative weights of every clone that remains at risk. Artificial-censoring membership changes as well, but only where the mismeasured variable enters the strategy, the eligibility rule or the censoring rule. item.evidence: This is the propagation the entry says is not done: a self-reported exposure is treated as mismeasured, sensitivity and specificity are given distributions rather than point values, and the correction is carried through the standardization to the reported interval. item.quote: The probabilistic bias analysis method (PBAM) using beta, logit-logistic, and triangular probability distributions for sensitivity/specificity to adjust for misclassification bias in self-reporting alcohol consumption and model-based standardization (MBS) to estimate the causal effect of alcohol consumption were used.

verdicts.reason: The paper combines misclassification sensitivity analysis with bootstrap sampling uncertainty, not several causal-bias mechanisms in one coherent analysis. Keeping random error separate from one measurement-bias model does not address joint violations of confounding, selection, measurement, and practical positivity.

item.problem_title: Sensitivity analyses vary one violated assumption at a time when several are violated together
item.problem_statement: A conventional emulation reports a point estimate under exchangeability, positivity and correct measurement, then a sensitivity analysis relaxing one of them. In a longitudinal emulation on routine data several are doubtful at once, and one-at-a-time analyses need not characterize their joint effect. Joint multi-bias analysis of confounding, selection and misclassification exists, with software, and so do longitudinal sensitivity models for sequential confounding. What is not standard, and not required by any reporting practice, is a joint region that also includes practical positivity failure under sustained-strategy g-methods, with the product of marginal analyses remaining the default in practice.
